note: Pushboys, cutters, pressers, fur workers. Garment and Fur Districts, daytime.

lines.text: Morning! Watch the rack, it bites.
Hey, you new? You look new. Everybody looks new at seven.
Six racks before coffee. Don't talk to me yet.
Thirty-Seventh Street. The only place a dress gets more exercise than me.
Cut forty pieces this morning. Perfect. Nobody claps.
Boss says the shop's moving south. South where? South of my rent?
In summer the furriers stand around like it's a wake. It is.
Truck's double-parked again. Every day, the same truck.
Piece rate went down. Pieces went up. That's math, they tell me.
Somebody's envelope is fatter than my paycheck.
Loft's a hundred degrees. Fans just move the hot around.
Rain! Cover the racks! Cover the racks!
Wet chiffon. My boss is gonna cry real tears.
Rain's the only thing that clears Seventh Avenue.
Ninety-five in the shade, and there's no shade.
Fur in July. Like selling snow shovels at Coney Island.
Yeah, yeah! Rack's got the right of way!
Honk all you want, I'm not a car!
You see a forty-foot rack and you honk? Genius!
Hey! You knocked the hems! Those are hems!
Watch it, pal, that's somebody's wedding dress.
Ow! My foot! My good foot!
Where's the fire? Lady's coat sale?
Slow down! This ain't the Garment Olympics!
Running in this heat? You'll melt like a mannequin.
Get that heap off the sidewalk!
You want to park? Park in Jersey!
Lights out on the cutting floor. Nobody move the knives.
Power's out. Finally a reason to stop.
Twelve hours. Twelve. My machine knows me better than my wife.
Union meeting Thursday. Bring your questions. Leave your boss.
You seen Dwayne? Kid owes me a sketch.
Hey, it's the guy who keeps walking into my racks.
You pushed my rack all the way to Thirty-Eighth. You want a job?
You! You stole a whole rack of coats! Feld's docking me for it!
Watch it! These dresses cost more than your shoes!
After what you did on Seventh, nobody's pushing anything near you.
Take the rack! Take it! It's all yours, it's polyester!
I don't want trouble. I got a union card and two kids at home.
Yeah, yeah. Go push your own rack.
Sorry? You owe me a dress. Two dresses.
